root_cause.text: The cachefiles_cull() function failed to account for a changed API contract in cachefiles_bury_object() that now expects 2 dentry references instead of 1, resulting in a reference count leak when only 1 reference was passed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch shows that commit 7bb1eb45e43c changed cachefiles_bury_object() to expect 2 references to the 'rep' dentry. Three callers were updated to use start_removing_dentry() which takes an extra reference, but cachefiles_cull() was overlooked and continued passing only 1 reference. The fix adds `dget(victim)` before the cachefiles_bury_object() call to provide the expected 2 references, with the function dropping one as intended.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add missing dget(victim) call to ensure correct reference counting for the dentry passed to cachefiles_bury_object().
intent_record.what: Added a dget(victim) call before cachefiles_bury_object() invocation, along with a comment explaining that cachefiles_bury_object() expects 2 references to 'victim' and drops one.
intent_record.how: This change increments the reference count of the 'victim' dentry before passing it to cachefiles_bury_object(). Since cachefiles_bury_object() internally drops one reference and the existing dput(victim) after the call drops another, this ensures the dentry maintains the correct reference count throughout the operation and is not prematurely freed.

bic_trace_step.reason: The cachefiles_cull() function calls cachefiles_bury_object() at line 479 with only one dentry reference (victim). However, examining cachefiles_bury_object(), the function expects to manage two dentry references: it performs dget(rep) at line 269 for non-directory objects and dput(rep) at line 272, but for directory objects it performs dput(grave) at line 395 without a corresponding dget on the 'rep' parameter. The function signature shows cachefiles_bury_object() takes 'dir' and 'rep' as separate dentry parameters. In cachefiles_cull(), only 'victim' is passed as 'rep' with no additional reference held. The vulnerability is that cachefiles_bury_object() now expects callers to provide 2 references to the dentry (one for the function's use, one for the caller to retain), but cachefiles_cull() only passes 1 reference, resulting in a reference count leak when the function consumes one of the references without the caller having provided an extra one.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit bd6ede8a06e89ca5a94a8b51cea792705d1b8ca2
Author: NeilBrown <neil@brown.name>
Date:   Thu Nov 13 11:18:28 2025 +1100

    VFS/nfsd/cachefiles/ovl: introduce start_removing() and end_removing()
    
    start_removing() is similar to start_creating() but will only return a
    positive dentry with the expectation that it will be removed.  This is
    used by nfsd, cachefiles, and overlayfs.  They are changed to also use
    end_removing() to terminate the action begun by start_removing().
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit shows that cachefiles_cull() has been updated to properly handle the new API contract. At line 815-816, after calling cachefiles_bury_object(), the code now performs `dput(victim)` to release the reference. This is correct because: (1) start_removing() at line 755 returns a dentry with one reference, (2) cachefiles_bury_object() now expects 2 references (it takes one via dget() at line 281 and releases one via end_removing()), (3) cachefiles_cull() must release its own reference via dput(victim) at line 815. The fix is present - the dput(victim) call ensures the caller's reference is properly released after bury_object() completes, preventing the reference count leak that would have occurred if only 1 reference was passed without this dput.
